sentences.text: Three distinct specimens of this animal have been reported, with the largest known individual estimated to be 2.2 meters long.
Its skull was proportionally large compared to other therizinosaurs, and four incomplete cervical vertebrae have been preserved in the fossil record.
Beipiaosaurus was approximately 2.2 meters long and 0.9 meters tall, making it the second largest known feathered dinosaur.
Preserved feather impressions allowed researchers to determine that it had brownish plumage, while the holotype preserves short, slender filamentous feathers on its left arm.
Before Yutyrannus was discovered, Beipiaosaurus were considered among the heaviest dinosaurs known to have direct evidence of feathers.
In 2018, scientists discovered fossilized skin flakes using a scanning electron microscope, revealing that non-avian dinosaurs shed their skin as dandruff, similar to extant birds and mammals.
The first remains were discovered in 1996 by a farmer named Li Yinxian near the village of Sihetun and formally described in 1999.

The specimen was collected from sediments deposited during the Aptian stage of the Cretaceous, and the type specimen is housed in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China.

Therizinosaurs, including Beipiaosaurus, are generally considered herbivorous based on their prosauropod-like teeth and body structure, though it is debated whether the front teeth were enlarged and conical like those of other therizinosaurs.

It is speculated that the finer feathers served as insulation and the larger feathers were ornamental, perhaps for social interactions like mating or communication, although researchers were unsure if they were for display or other functions.
Studies suggest the paleoenvironment of the Yixian Formation had seasonal climate fluctuations, being warm and humid with dry seasons where the environment became more arid.

Beipiaosaurus is classified as a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs, and features suggest that all therizinosauroids are coelurosaurian theropods, rather than sauropodomorphs or ornithischians.

Beipiaosaurus was originally assigned to Therizinosauroidea in a basal position by Xu et al. in 1999, and was definitively placed within the Theropoda, specifically as a maniraptoran, due to theropod features and feather impressions found in its holotype.

Beipiaosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Barremian age, at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago between the Barremian and Aptian stages.
The flora of the Yixian Formation was dominated by conifers, ferns, cycads, and horsetails, including conifers related to modern species found mainly in subtropical and temperate highland forests.

It is debated whether the front teeth of Beipiaosaurus were enlarged and conical like those of other therizinosaurs, and in a 2009 interview, Xu stated that neither type of feather was definitely for flight and researchers were unsure if they were for display or other functions.
